description:
A security team is investigating a suspected rogue device on the corporate network. You need to inventory all layer-2 devices observed in recent packet captures.

Analyze these four capture files in ~/Documents/captures/:
- http.cap
- dns.cap
- telnet-cooked.pcap
- smtp.pcap

For each file, extract all unique source and destination MAC addresses. For every unique MAC address found across all four files, determine:
1. The hardware vendor/manufacturer (OUI lookup)
2. Total packets where it appears as source
3. Total packets where it appears as destination
4. Which capture file(s) it appears in

Also identify the single MAC address that sent the most packets overall (most active sender) and count the total number of unique MAC addresses.

Save your report to ~/Documents/captures/mac_inventory_report.txt in this format:

=== MAC Address Network Inventory Report ===

Total unique MAC addresses: <N>
Most active sender: <MAC> (<vendor>) with <count> packets sent

--- Per-Device Inventory ---
MAC: <address>
Vendor: <vendor_name>
Packets Sent: <count>
Packets Received: <count>
Seen In: <file1>, <file2>, ...

MAC: <address>
...

Use Wireshark, tshark, or any available tools to complete this analysis. Make sure MAC addresses are in colon-separated format (e.g., 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e).
